=== I MUTATION-PROBED EVERY CLAIMED FIX. NONE OF THE CHECKS IS VACUOUS. ===

Each mutation applied to the working tree, suite re-run, file restored, `git status --porcelain` verified empty afterwards. A check that still passes when you break what it guards is worthless, and this repo has shipped several, so I broke all seven:

  M1 revert `on:` to `check_suite:` (the original defect)          -> 2 failed
  M2 replace the find step's run: with `echo "prs=" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT` -> 1 failed
  M3 drop the B1 loop fix (`|| rc=1` and `exit "$rc"`)             -> 1 failed
  M4 let an unresolvable TARGETED event fall through to the sweep  -> 1 failed
  M5 drop the isdigit() validation on the dispatch pr_number       -> 2 failed
  M6 send NOTICE diagnostics back to stdout                        -> 1 failed
  M7 trust workflow_run.pull_requests instead of commits/{sha}/pulls -> 3 failed

M1 and M2 matter most: tests/test_workflows_parse.py asserts against the PARSED YAML structure (`yaml.safe_load`, and correctly `data.get(True)` for YAML 1.1's implicit `on` -> boolean coercion), not against file text. This is precisely the vacuous-check trap this repo is documented to have shipped before -- a string search that matched the comment warning about the hazard. These tests cannot be fooled that way: auto-queue.yml's comments mention "check_suite" five times, and the assertion `"check_suite" not in on` still passes on the real file and still fails on M1.

M6 is the "could not check vs checked and found nothing" shape, handled correctly: _api() returns None on failure and every caller treats None as unresolved rather than as an empty result, and the NOTICE text goes to stderr specifically because stdout is appended to $GITHUB_OUTPUT where a line without "=" would make the runner fail the step. M4 is the same shape one level up and is the best single piece of engineering in this diff: an unreadable payload on a TARGETED trigger returns None rather than silently widening into a repo-wide sweep.

=== TWO MINOR FINDINGS ===

F1. `manual_str.isdigit()` is the wrong predicate for "is this an integer I can int()". Python's str.isdigit() is true for non-ASCII digit characters, and the two halves of that set behave differently:
   - '²' (SUPERSCRIPT TWO): isdigit() is True, int() RAISES ValueError. Reproduced against the shipped function: `resolve_pr_numbers({'inputs':{'pr_number':'²'}}, 'workflow_dispatch')` raises ValueError, uncaught. emit_find_prs()'s docstring promises that a lookup failure prints `prs=` and returns 0 so the 15-minute sweep retries; instead the step dies nonzero. The contract and the behaviour disagree.
   - '١٢٣' (Arabic-Indic digits): isdigit() is True and int() SUCCEEDS, returning [123]. A dispatch input that does not read as "123" to a human silently resolves to PR #123.
   Severity LOW: workflow_dispatch requires repo write access, and the first case fails loudly rather than silently, which is the better of the two failure modes. But this is a validator that does not validate what it is documented to validate. `manual_str.isascii() and manual_str.isdigit()` fixes both, or a try/except around int(). I did NOT find a shell-injection path: because the value is int()'d before it reaches the `prs=` line, `${{ steps.find.outputs.prs }}` in the "Enqueue if ready" run: block cannot carry attacker-controlled text. I checked that specifically, since that step holds secrets.AUTO_TOKEN_QUEUE.

F2. proof/64.json's `commit` field (6385feb9eb4d54b9ec62ec3e4e65cb0246f48de1) is not merely unreachable from this branch -- `git cat-file -e` shows the object does not exist in this repository at all, so no reader can resolve it. The record DECLARES this in `unproven`, which is genuinely honest and is why this is an observation rather than a charge. But the justification given there overstates the constraint: it argues a proof record "can never state its own final commit sha", which is true only if the field must name the record's own commit. It need not. The sibling PR #46's proof record names the last commit touching the DELIVERABLE (ba983cf), which is both meaningful and reachable; the equivalent here is 22e75ff ("Re-cut #48: carry forward the auto-queue trigger + loop-abort fix"). Recording that instead would be resolvable and would cost nothing. Worth noting for the gate too: lwb_check_proof.py passes a record whose `commit` names a nonexistent object, so nothing mechanical catches this.

=== ONE UNRESOLVED CI ITEM, recorded rather than explained away ===

On 94c32ff all six `test` legs are red. On five of them the ONLY failing step is "lwb-lanes" -- the by-design 0-reviews state this record clears. On ONE leg, test (windows-latest, 3.12), the step "Unit / adapter / conformance tests" ALSO failed.

I could not determine why, and I am deliberately NOT calling it a flake:
 - Actions job LOG blobs return 403 through this container's proxy. I have step conclusions and nothing below them.
 - Not reproducible here: Linux/CPython 3.11 only, 628 passed serially, twice (once as `pytest tests/ -q`, once as CI's bare `pytest -q`). I did not run Windows, macOS, 3.10 or 3.12.
 - CI runs plain `python -m pytest -q` with no xdist, so a parallel-safety race between tests is NOT the explanation. I checked that specifically, because a previous reviewer documented tests/test_lwb_check_state_claims.py as parallel-unsafe.
 - CROSS-PR EVIDENCE, measured in this same run: the sibling PR #46 shows the identical pattern on a DIFFERENT platform -- test (macos-latest, 3.12) also failing its test step, five other legs failing only at lwb-lanes. Both are 3.12. origin/main (0d1be71) is green on all six legs, and PRs #63, #62, #58, #51 and #45 currently show no failing test legs at all.
Two unrelated PRs failing the same step on different platforms, both on 3.12, with main green, is evidence that the failure is NOT attributable to either PR's content -- which is why it does not change my verdict. It is not evidence of what the cause IS. Someone with log access should look at a 3.12 leg before merging; this record clears lwb-lanes and cannot turn that leg green.

=== ONE BEHAVIOURAL WIDENING THE OWNER SHOULD SEE (not a fault) ===

The schedule sweep resolves EVERY open PR targeting main -- 20 today -- and runs auto_queue.py against each, every 15 minutes, under a 5-minute job timeout. That is the intended self-heal and it is documented as such. It is safe by construction: enqueue only happens when every REQUIRED context is green, lwb-lanes runs inside the required `test` job, so a PR lacking a valid independent review record is red and cannot be auto-enqueued. I confirmed the required-contexts list above. I did NOT measure the sweep's wall-clock against 20 PRs, so whether it fits in timeout-minutes: 5 at today's PR count is unverified. The concurrency group falls back to github.run_id for the sweep, so two overlapping sweeps do not serialize against each other; the comment acknowledges this deliberately.
